facts.text: In 1828, the settlement of Savageville was renamed Providence when its post office opened, a change that honored settlers’ gratitude for divine protection.
Richard Savage, a Virginian, opened a general store that became the nucleus of Providence, the city that grew around his shop.
Commercial coal mining started in 1888, and every June Providence celebrates its mining heritage with an annual Coal Festival.
In 1993, the Providence Commercial Historic District was created to honor the historic downtown buildings that define the city’s architectural heritage.
Situated in Kentucky’s Black Patch tobacco region, Providence rose to become the third‑largest stemming market in the United States.
The Tradewater River runs just west of Providence, and the city centers around the crossroads of Kentucky Routes 109 and 120.
